text: This is a guide for the Landesamt für Einwanderung, the immigration office in Berlin. To apply for a residence permit, read my residence permit guide instead. How to apply for a residence permit

title: To apply for a residence permit
text: Some residence permits have their own online application form: Opportunity card Student visa Blue Card Work visa for people with a university degree Work visa for people with professional training Freelance visa Citizenship Permanent residence For Blue Card holders For the family of German citizens For skilled workers For refugees and asylum seekers EU permanent residence ( what’s the difference?) For Blue Card holders For the family of German citizens For skilled workers For refugees and asylum seekers EU permanent residence ( what’s the difference?) See the full list If your residence permit is not in this list, use the contact form to send your application.

title: Use the contact form
text: To contact the Ausländerbehörde, or to apply for a residence permit that is not in this list, you must… Find your department Use the contact form Find your department’s contact form. Write in German. If you don’t speak German, use Deepl. If it’s urgent, use the emergency form. Your message must include… Your name and date of birth What you need The expiration date of your visa or residence permit If your visa or residence permit expires soon, ask for a Fiktionsbescheinigung Your name and date of birth What you need The expiration date of your visa or residence permit If your visa or residence permit expires soon, ask for a Fiktionsbescheinigung Attach your documents Add your application documents to your message. Complete applications are processed faster. You can only upload 5 small files. Use PDF files or photos, nothing else. If you have too many documents, merge them and make them smaller. If you still have too many documents, mail them. Send your message If you get an error ( Anti-Spam-Schutz), it’s because you took too long to send your message. Click the back button, and send it again. After you send the message, click Zusammenfassung ausdrucken to print the confirmation message. This is a proof of your residence permit application. You might not get a confirmation email. Wait for a response They reply very slowly. If you wait more than 3 months, you can sue the Ausländerbehörde. If your visa or resident permit expires, it’s usually extended until the Ausländerbehörde processes your application. Sometimes, you can’t reply to their emails directly, so you must use the contact form again. What happens next?

title: Other contact options
text: You can contact the Ausländerbehörde by registered mail, but it’s not better or faster. You can’t call or fax them. Address your letter to the correct department, at the correct address: Friedrich-Krause-Ufer or Keplerstraße. How to mail a letter

title: Emergencies
text: If it’s urgent, choose the Eiliger Termin/Notfall category in the contact form.

title: Locations
text: In Berlin, there are 3 immigration office locations. Choose the correct one. Friedrich-Krause-Ufer Keplerstraße Fasanenstraße (Business Immigration Service)

title: Departments
text: The Berlin immigration office has multiple departments. Send your application to the correct one. B1, B2, B3, B4 For skilled workers, students, researchers and their family. They handle Blue Cards, work visas, student visas and more. B6 – Business Immigration Service (BIS) For skilled workers and their family. They handle Blue Cards and work visas. They are usually faster than other departments. F1, F2 For privileged countries. They handle permanent residence, freelance visas, and everything else. M1, M2, M3, M4 For everyone else. They handle permanent residence, freelance visas, and everything else. Choose the department that is responsible for your country. S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6 For citizenship applications. Choose the department that is responsible for your country. List of departments Wait times by department

To visit the Ausländerbehörde, you need an appointment. If you go without an appointment, they will not help you. You can’t book an appointment yourself. You must apply for a residence permit or use their contact form. They decide when they give you an appointment. They usually take months to reply.

It takes 3 to 6 months to get a residence permit in Berlin. The wait times vary by department and residence permit type. Ausländerbehörde wait times Usually, you can’t start working before you get your residence permit. It might be cheaper to apply in your home country, and move to Berlin after you get permission to work. You don’t need to wait in Berlin without an income. How to apply in your country You don’t need a residence permit to start studying. You can start studying as soon as you arrive in Germany. Tell us how long it took to apply for a residence permit in Berlin. This tool requires JavaScript to work.

At the Ausländerbehörde, you can pay with Visa, Mastercard, cash or Girocard. When you apply for a residence permit online, you sometimes need to pay in advance, during your application. You can pay with Visa, Mastercard or PayPal. You can’t pay with cash or Girocard.

title: How to pay your application fees
text: At the end of your appointment, you get a plastic payment card ( Kassenkarte). Bring it to a payment machine ( Kassenautomat). Follow the signs to find it. These machines accept cash, EC cards, Visa and Mastercard. If your card is not accepted, get cash from an ATM. After you have paid, you can go home. You don’t need to go back to your case worker. The fee for a Blue Card, work visa or freelance visa is tax-deductible, so keep the receipt. Citizenship application fees are not tax-deductible.

The Ausländerbehörde has 3 months to process your residence permit application. If it takes longer, you can sue them. It costs € 700 to € 3,000. Suing does not always work. The Ausländerbehörde sometimes ignores court orders. File an Untätigkeitsklage against the Ausländerbehörde. This tool requires JavaScript to work. First, your lawyer sends a scary letter to the Ausländerbehörde. The Ausländerbehörde wants to avoid a lawsuit, so they process your application faster. If the scary letter does not work, you can sue the Ausländerbehörde. The legal system is slow, so a lawsuit can take months or years. If you win, the Ausländerbehörde must pay for your legal fees. Usually, the Ausländerbehörde reacts before your case goes to court, so you must pay your own legal fees. In other words, you pay a few hundred euros, and things sometimes go faster. A lawyer can pressure the Ausländerbehörde, but they can’t help you skip the queue. In other cities, threatening to sue the Ausländerbehörde can make things worse. The Ausländerbehörde can become very strict, ask for more documents, and make your application even slower. Find an immigration lawyer

The immigration office does not give immigration advice. An immigration lawyer or a relocation consultant can answer your questions. You can also get free advice from some organisations.
